scope: Methods used in a conditional optical screen. Source access is recorded individually; manuscript source admission remains separate.

sources.citation: CIE (2002), CIE Equations for Disability Glare, CIE 146:2002, in CIE 146/147:2002.
sources.access: Official public description read; full paid report not accessed.
sources.use: Eye-plane illuminance and angle conventions; age-adjusted formula valid strictly between 1 and 30 degrees. Broader angular formulas are not implemented.

sources.citation: Vos, J. J. (2003), On the cause of disability glare and its dependence on glare angle, age and ocular pigmentation, Clinical and Experimental Optometry 86(6), 363-370.
sources.access: Author's abstract read through PubMed; equation and validity range are explicitly given there. Full paper not read.

sources.citation: CIE (2024), Assessment of Discomfort Glare from Daylight in Buildings, CIE 252:2024.
sources.access: Official public description read; full paid report not accessed.
sources.use: Separate contrast and total-amount discomfort effects; respect each metric's validation domain. No outdoor discomfort threshold is taken from this report.

sources.citation: Wienold, J. and Christoffersen, J. (2006), Evaluation methods and development of a new glare prediction model for daylight environments with the use of CCD cameras, Energy and Buildings 38, 743-757.
sources.access: Author institution record and original-paper PDF sections on the fitted equation and validity inspected; full-source editorial review outstanding.
sources.use: Indoor office experiment and DGP validation limits; prevents interpreting an extrapolated outdoor score as a probability.

sources.citation: Pharr, M., Jakob, W. and Humphreys, G., Physically Based Rendering, 4th edition, Specular Reflection and Transmission.
sources.access: Author-maintained book section, dielectric Fresnel equations inspected.
sources.use: Unpolarized dielectric Fresnel reflection. Water index 1.333 is an imposed scenario.

sources.citation: Cox, C. and Munk, W. (1954), Measurement of the Roughness of the Sea Surface from Photographs of the Sun's Glitter, JOSA 44(11), 838-850.
sources.access: Publisher abstract/record inspected; full paper not read.
sources.use: Method lead for rough-water glint. No Earth wind-to-slope relation is transferred to the Moon.

sources.citation: Pharr, M., Jakob, W. and Humphreys, G., Physically Based Rendering, 4th edition, The Light Transport Equation and A Simple Path Tracer.
sources.access: Author-maintained chapters inspected for the surface rendering equation, path throughput, separate delta-source evaluation, and analytic-limit checks.
sources.use: Neutral Lambertian surface transport with cosine-weighted paths and a separately evaluated collimated Sun; independently implemented small-scene integrator.
